Answer: F
Reason: The axial CT (Figure 2) demonstrates an ill-defined parenchymal consolidation in the posterior aspect of the left lower lobe (apical/superior segment) with associated narrowing of the feeding segmental bronchus and no significant mediastinal lymphadenopathy. This radiographic pattern, particularly the bronchial narrowing without nodal enlargement in a smoker, is characteristic of bronchiolitis obliterans organizing pneumonia (BOOP), distinguishing it from malignancy or tuberculosis which typically present with lymphadenopathy or cavitation.
